Why Choose a London Campus of a UK University?

Many UK universities run campuses in London that are separate from their main city. These campuses often have smaller classes, flexible start dates and a focus on business, computing, health and hospitality. They can also be less expensive than the large central London universities.

The trade-off is that facilities and course choice may be narrower than at the main campus. Always check what is taught in London and what is taught elsewhere.

What to Check Before You Apply

  • Where the course is taught: confirm that your whole program runs in London.
  • Intake dates: January and May intakes usually have earlier deadlines than you expect.
  • Degree awarded by: confirm which institution awards your degree and how it is recognized.
  • Graduate Route: ask the university to confirm your course counts toward post-study work rights.
  • Visa record: look at how the university handles sponsor compliance, because refusal rates affect its ability to recruit.

Visa Funds for London

Studying in London means the higher maintenance rate: £1,529 per month now (£13,761 for nine months), rising to £1,570 (£14,130) from 30 November 2026, plus your unpaid tuition. This applies to London campuses too, so budget for it even if the university is on the outskirts.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are London campuses of UK universities good value?
Often, but fees and course quality vary. Compare total cost, teaching hours and graduate outcomes.
Do London campus students get the same degree?
Usually the degree is awarded by the parent university, but confirm this in writing before you accept an offer.
Can I start in January or May?
Many London campuses offer these intakes. Check each course page for dates and deadlines.
